newsitem.title: UK: IEA regrets U.S. plan to sell $209 mln oil stocks.
newsitem.headline: IEA regrets U.S. plan to sell $209 mln oil stocks.

text.p: Robert Priddle, Director of the International Energy Agency (IEA) in Paris, said on Friday he "regrets" the approval of a plan by a U.S. House of Representative's committee to sell $209 million worth of oil from America's Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
The IEA, the West's oil "watchdog" founded in 1974 after the first oil price shock, administers an emergency plan to protect its 24 member countries against future energy crises.
Under the plan IEA members maintain emergency stocks equal to at least 90 days net oil imports.
In an emergency participants are pledged to share those stocks where necessary.
"Earlier U.S. government stocks were over 90 days. Now we calculate they are under 70 days. That's quite a drop," said Priddle.

On Thursday, the U.S. House Appropriations Committee approved a plan to sell $209 million in oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) in fiscal year 1998. The sale would be made under a $13 billion spending bill for energy and lands programs.
The income would be used to cover the cost of administering the reserves.
The committee rejected an amendment to sell another $89 million in SPR oil to help keep the National Endowment for the Arts alive.
However, Republicans from the House Commerce Committee, which is in charge of authorizing SPR oil sales, planned to introduce an amendment on the House floor to strip the oil auction out of the bill.
In the 1997 fiscal year, the United States sold $220 million of SPR oil, the IEA said.
Earlier this month the German government confirmed reports that it was considering selling 7.3 million tonnes of its oil reserves.
Besides government held SPR, oil companies in both countries maintain significant oil stocks which may be called upon in an emergency.
